merger_name: Tasmanian Department of Health – leasehold interest in vacant site at Hobart International Airport

acquirers.name: The Crown in Right of Tasmania (acting through the Department of Health)

party_page.name: The Crown in Right of Tasmania (acting through the Department of Health)

anzsic_codes.name: Airport Operations and Other Air Transport Support Services

merger_description:
The Crown in Right of Tasmania acting through the Tasmanian Department of Health (**TDoH**) is proposing to acquire a leasehold interest in land located in the aviation support precinct at Hobart International Airport from Hobart International Airport Pty Ltd (Hobart Airport).

The TDoH is part of the state government of Tasmania. TDoH is proposing to use the land to construct a new TDoH production kitchen facility comprising of a commercial kitchen, administrative office space and on-site parking (the Production Kitchen). The Production Kitchen will replace the existing kitchen facility operated by TDoH at the northern end of the airport passenger terminal building. The parties are proposing to relocate the kitchen facility as the location of the existing kitchen is impeding future terminal development.

TDoH will continue to provide catering services to Southern Hospitals and a variety of other hospitals, currently serving as the primary supplier of food for the Royal Hobart Hospital. TDoH provides between 1600 to 1800 plated meals a day to various government and privately owned facilities.

Hobart International Airport was privatised in 1998 with Hobart International Airport Pty Ltd entering into a 99-year lease with the Commonwealth Government. As of 2019, a consortium consisting of Queensland Investment Corporation and Royal Schiphol Group holds a 70% equity interest in Hobart Airport and Care Super holds the remaining 30%.

The parties are proposing to enter into a 20-year lease, with an option to extend for an additional 10 years.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
certain publicly available information, and had regard to the factors
in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010
(Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the Acquisition involves the relocation and expansion of the
kitchen facility from one area of the Hobart International
Airport to another, and would not result in any horizontal
consolidation or the removal of a competitor
b. there appear to be alternative providers of catering services,
and other sites available for providers of these services, in
the area around Hobart International Airport.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
